structure.title: Chapters 1–4 · Before Niels can remember
structure.text: Jacobsen begins with the parents' unequal appetites for poetry and ordinary life. Their child inherits a house full of dreams before he can invent his own. His devotion to his aunt Edele gives imagination an object whose life extends well beyond what the boy can see.

structure.title: Chapters 5–11 · The artist among friends
structure.text: In company Niels can debate belief and imagine the poetry he will write. Erik actually leaves to work as an artist. As friendship and desire bring their lives closer together, the habit of contemplating an action acquires a price other people may have to pay.

structure.title: Chapters 12–14 · Home and the claims of grief
structure.text: Travel gives way to the management of a farm and the demands of family life. What atheism meant in a conversation among clever adults differs from what it can mean beside a sickbed, where another person's fear may matter more than one's own consistency.

people.name: Niels Lyhne
people.text: Niels can picture a future feeling so vividly that anticipation almost takes the place of experience. His gift gives the novel much of its beauty. It also helps explain why a project that occupies him for years might leave so little on paper.

people.name: Edele and Fennimore
people.text: A child's adoration of his aunt and a grown man's desire for his friend's wife are very different attachments. In both, what Niels can imagine about a woman sometimes fills the space where he might have heard what she wants.

context.title: Losing the language of prayer
context.text: To give up belief here also means giving up a way of appealing for help, thanking someone and sharing grief. The people closest to Niels do not have to accept that loss on the same terms. A question of conviction can come between two people who love one another.

notice.text: Notice when an imagined conversation has already happened for Niels.
notice.why: He can enter an encounter carrying the whole emotional weight of a scene nobody else has lived through. The person meeting him has to begin from quite another point.

notice.text: Watch the years disappear between chapters.
notice.why: A long description can hold a feeling almost still. Then a new chapter casually reports the passage of years. The difference lets us feel the gap between the intensity of Niels's hopes and the fraction of a lifetime in which he might realise them.

opening: Niels Lyhne imagines a life large enough for poetry, love, and freedom from the beliefs he inherited. He is better at imagining it than at living it. The women he desires have lives beyond the roles he gives them, and conviction becomes harder to sustain when grief demands something conviction cannot provide. Jacobsen stays close to the exquisite feelings and evasions of a gifted dreamer, making it possible to recognise the waste of a life without dismissing the person wasting it.
